entries.text: I didn't sleep well last night, so this morning I was walking slowly to the station. My brother Daniel was already waiting there with two coffees. "You look tired," he said. "It's the neighbours' fault," I answered. They're painting their house, and the noise started before dawn. We laughed, caught the 7:45 train, and talked about the holidays we'd planned for next summer.

entries.text: Bees are surprisingly clever insects. A single colony can contain 50,000 workers, and each one has a job: some collect nectar, others clean the hive, and a few guard the entrance. When a scout finds a rich field of flowers, she returns and performs a waggle dance that shows her sisters the direction and the distance. Scientists studying these well-known dances have learned that the longer the dance lasts, the farther away the food is.

"Where have you been?" asked Maria.
"At the library," said Tom. "I borrowed three books about gardening."
"Gardening? You've never planted anything in your life!"
"That's true, but my grandmother left me her old garden, and I'd like to grow tomatoes there. Do you think it will work?"
Maria smiled. "Honestly, I don't know. Let's try together this weekend."

entries.text: The city council announced on Monday that public transport fares will rise by 4% next year. Mayor Johnson said the money would be used to buy 120 new electric buses and to repair older stations. Dr. Smith, who studies urban planning at the University of Leeds, believes cheaper tickets would bring more passengers. Residents can read the full proposal at https://example.com/council/fares or send questions to help@example.com before the vote on March 3rd.

entries.text: The old lighthouse stood on the highest rock, looking over a restless grey sea. Every evening the keeper climbed the narrow stairs, lit the lamp, and watched the ships passing by. He had grown quieter with the years, but his eyes were sharper than anyone's in the village. Storms came and went, boats were lost and found, and the light kept burning brighter and steadier than the stars above it.
